blockers.description: Owner rejected the current Houdini scene visually; it must not be deployed to QA.
blockers.workaround: Produce local Houdini and Three.js review renders plus the visual spec, correct the scene, and request visual approval before QA release.

blockers.description: The current completion algorithm filters placement by roomId, but passage tiles inherit adjacent room IDs, so room props can land in corridors.
blockers.workaround: Constrain non-corridor assets to exact zoneId and use explicit corridor-safe wall fixture sockets.

human_actions_pending.action: Review side-by-side local renders after corrections
human_actions_pending.context: Owner requires the Houdini source scene and Three.js runtime to match the accepted Diablo-style atmosphere before QA deployment.

decisions.decision: Pause QA deployment immediately after owner visual rejection.
decisions.rationale: The current scene has semantically incorrect placements and inconsistent presentation.

decisions.decision: Review locally in both Houdini and Three.js before deployment.
decisions.rationale: Deployment is not required for accurate material, lighting, fire, shadow, fog, and asset-presence review.

decisions.decision: Keep the 150 MB hard cap for production but make it report-only for qa and PRs targeting qa.
decisions.rationale: QA must accept the complete review kit while production still needs an enforced size safeguard.

decisions.decision: Randomize approved prop sets among semantic sockets, never arbitrary walkable tiles.
decisions.rationale: Randomization must preserve traversal, readability, and plausible placement.

next_action: Read .planning/.continue-here.md, acknowledge its blocking constraints, then create the visual acceptance spec and render the current hipnc plus local Three.js environment=houdini baseline before changing placements.
